title: Model reference resolution hierarchy and override semantics (tag / semver / commit-hash / alias)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need predictable, auditable semantics for resolving model references in the Redwood API/SDK. We currently accept multiple forms of model identifiers (tag aliases, semver-like release labels, commit hashes, and ephemeral experimental tags) but behavior is underspecified in edge cases: mixing aliases with semver, tag collisions across model families, and runtime fallbacks under capacity pressure. This ambiguity causes surprising rollouts and complicates Dedicated/Private deployments where pin stability is required.

Proposal: Define a single resolution hierarchy and explicit override rules implemented by the API resolver and mirrored in SDK clients. Key elements: 1) canonical identifier resolution order, 2) deterministic tie-breaking, 3) explicit override semantics (force-hash, prefer-latest, tag-then-semver), 4) experimental tag handling (short-lived, requires opt-in), 5) runtime fallback policy and telemetry, 6) error and warning contract for ambiguous pins. The resolver should be deterministic across hosted/dedicated/private environments and provide machine-readable explanations (resolution_trace) in responses/headers when requested.

Resolution hierarchy (proposed):
- Exact commit hash (full-length or canonical short) — highest precedence; resolves only to that exact artifact.
- Fully qualified release semver (major.minor.patch[@buildmeta]) — resolves to a matching immutable release.
- Tag alias (stable tags like "latest", "redwood-stable", or customer-defined aliases) — resolves to latest release matching alias mapping in model catalog.
- Floating semver ranges (e.g., ^1.2, >=2.0 <3.0) — resolves using catalog's release index with deterministic sorting rules.
- Experimental/ephemeral tags (exp-*, canary-*) — only allowed when client opt-in header present; lowest precedence and may be rejected in Dedicated by policy.

Override rules: specifying force=true with a non-hash identifier should escalate to resolving then pinning the resolved commit-hash and return the canonical hash to the caller. SDK convenience: an API call 'resolve_and_pin' that returns canonical ref + checksum and caches locally. If a request includes multiple identifiers (e.g., tag + semver), we will reject with 400 unless the client provides an explicit 'selector_priority' array.

Runtime fallback policy: Runtime may fallback to compatible variants if the pinned artifact is unavailable (e.g., quantized variant, older patch) only if the request includes allow_fallback=true and the client is aware (response includes fallback_reason and fallback_original_ref). Defaults: hosted API: allow_fallback=false; Dedicated default follows customer config; Private follows on-prem policy. Any fallback must emit telemetry and a per-request warning header.

Developer ergonomics: SDKs should expose: resolveModel(ref, options) -> {canonical: string, trace: string[], warnings: string[]}, pinModel(ref) (idempotent), and a strictPin(ref) that errors if resolution does not return an immutable commit-hash. Server should support query param ?resolution_trace=1 to include machine-readable trace in JSON response or X-Redwood-Resolution-Trace header for streaming responses.

Telemetry & auditing: Every resolution must log: input_ref, resolved_ref (commit hash), resolution_path, resolver_version, decision_timestamp, and resolver_node_id. Store mappings in catalog with TTL for ephemeral tags. Provide Console view for pin drift and recent alias updates.

Backward compatibility: Existing clients that pass simple strings will continue to work with the new hierarchy, but we will add deprecation warnings when a floating-range or ambiguous selector is used without explicit selector_priority. Migration guide will show how to switch to strictPin and resolve_and_pin flow.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement resolver server-side with feature flag (resolver_v2) + telemetry, 2) SDK updates (python/js/java) to consume resolution_trace and expose convenience methods, 3) Beta this behavior for a subset of orgs, 4) enable deprecation warnings globally after 4 weeks, 5) flip default stricter behaviors in runtime-2.4 release.

Security/Privacy considerations: canonical commit hashes are stable and safe to expose; experimental tags should not leak internal build metadata. Resolver must sanitize build metadata before returning public traces.
acceptance_criteria: Resolver implements hierarchy: hash > exact semver > alias tag > semver range > experimental
API returns canonical commit-hash for pinning when requested
SDKs provide resolveModel and strictPin methods with matching behavior
Runtime fallback respects allow_fallback flag and emits telemetry and headers
Console shows pin drift events for aliases with timestamps
Deprecation warnings emitted for ambiguous selectors in API responses
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha: Created ticket after PM sync; initial proposal drafted. Linked to onboarding playbook in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/company/model-onboarding (internal).

2026-03-02 Liam: Implemented prototype resolver v2 in branch feat/resolver-hierarchy. Added unit tests for semver ranges and exact-hash precedence. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7112
2026-03-03 Rui (PM): Requested explicit error codes for ambiguous multi-selector inputs. Suggested HTTP 400 with code RESOLVER_AMBIGUOUS_SELECTORS and human message. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-04 Design review (Maya): UX for resolution_trace header reviewed. Recommended compact base64-encoded JSON for streaming paths and full JSON for Console/API.

2026-03-05 QA: Began smoke tests against Dedicated staging cluster; observed one failing case where alias mapping had circular update — added guard to catalog update path. Test run: https://internal-ci.redwood/jobs/21345
